title: Emil Parra as MC
summary: Coquille describes Emil Parra as the best MC, a dancer who leapt off pianos and later worked at Pat O'Brien's.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, when you played these jobs, would anybody ever have an MC or anything like that?

Well, in the old days, quite often we'd play for a big dance in the tea room and there'd be five acts of floor shows. We'd have to play for the five acts of the floor show. I don't know if you remember the late Emil Parra. Oh yeah. I sang for years and years at Pat O'Brien's. I knew him there. Emil Parra. Well, let me tell you, Emil Parra was always an MC and he was one of the greatest MCs in New Orleans that I've ever seen. And every time we had five acts of floor shows, a play after the dance, or maybe during the middle of the party they'd put on five acts of shows, you know, girl dancers or whatever, you're a magician or whatever have you. Well, Emil Parra always had the job of being the MC for the floor show. This was before he went to Pat O'Brien's, now this is way back. And Emil was a marvelous dancer and marvelous MC. And he used to always wind up his act by getting on top of the baby grand piano and jumping way up in the air and almost landing on his back. I used to get scared to death every time he did that. But he'd never miss. And he was so full of vim, vigor, and vitality. He was personality plus. That's why he was later hired at Pat O'Brien, where he remained for years until he passed away.
Did he? He must have been in the 50s when he passed. I would imagine that around the time. Somewhere around that time.
I would imagine that around the time. Somewhere around that time.
Anyway, he'd jump off the top of the piano and he'd land on the piano or the floor. And not only jump off the piano.

When he jumped off the piano, I don't care if it was an upright or a baby grand, he would jump up in the air three or four feet down to the dance floor and, you know, land his back would miss the floor that much, you know, like two inches. And he'd never miss. And it used to frighten me to death every time he did that. And he'd just pop right up on his feet? Pop right up. Oh, he was a good athlete, I guess. And a marvelous dancer.
See, I never saw him do any of that. All I ever saw him do was sing and dance.

He was about the best MC in New Orleans that I've seen during my career, you know. Did he ever tell any jokes? No, but he knew how to talk to people. He knew how to get people to liven up a party. He was never at a loss for words, let's put it that way.

He was like this with his talk. He wouldn't give people a chance to say no or anything, man. I mean, they were out on the floor. If nobody was dancing quick enough, Emile would have been dancing in five minutes. He just full of that vim, vigor and vitality, plus personality, plus. And he knew how to liven up the deadest party you ever saw. He could liven it up in five minutes.
He must have been on the day. And he did great at Pat O'Brien's.

He was a real asset at Pat O'Brien's. And, you know, being at Pat O'Brien's all those years. Now, of course, Emile had traveled all over the country before he ever come down here. Emile was very popular. And working all those years at Pat O'Brien's, Emile knew every college song in the United States. I don't think there was any college song in the United States that Emile didn't know the words to. And he was about the only one in New Orleans that could really sing all the college songs that I knew of.
Well, do you think he wasn't from New Orleans? No, I think he was from New Orleans. Yeah, but he traveled.
He did extensive traveling before all of that. Yeah, he did a lot of traveling.
He once told me he was a Creole. But that could mean, you know, you could be from another place and be a Creole. Probably so. I would imagine he's from New Orleans.

He lived up in Carrollton somewhere. I even remember that it was Carrollton. I couldn't point out the house, but he lived in Carrollton. That was another great loss to the end of the year. He was a great loss to the entertainment field. He had such great, he was like Gerard. He had so much personality. Yeah.
